caveats: Manual probe, not a `doflow worker run` record and not a `worker --action evidence` check. A person ran `codex exec -s workspace-write` and, without a model call, `codex sandbox -c 'sandbox_mode="workspace-write"' /bin/zsh -c 'echo x > <path>/probe.txt'` once per path, then listed the directory to confirm the file was absent or present.
Only nine paths were tried (the nine in `tried`). A path name not in that list is untested, so `protectedPaths` may be incomplete.
The denial was observed on macOS (seatbelt) as `operation not permitted`. Other operating systems were not tried.
The `exec -s workspace-write` runs were read from the agent's text report; a sandbox-denied command produced no `command_execution` item in `--json` output.
A nested `sub/.git` was writable, so a protected name blocks only at the workspace root; the matcher in src/runtime/worker/protected-paths.ts matches a declared path's first segment only.
